title: Mattathias
hook: a priest in Modi'in refuses to sacrifice to idols, and the revolt begins

segments.voice: Yesterday, a mother watched seven sons refuse, and spoke courage to every one. Your line was she encouraged them. Today, a priest says no out loud.

Modi'in is a town, not the capital. The first book of Maccabees says a priest named Mattathias lives there with his five sons: John, Simon, Judas who is called Maccabeus, Eleazar and Jonathan. He has been mourning what's happening in Jerusalem, tearing his clothes, putting on sackcloth. Then the king's officers come to make the town sacrifice to idols, and they go straight to him, because he's a leader there. Their offer is friendly: go first, set the example, and you and your sons will be counted among the king's friends, rewarded with silver and gold. Everyone in town is watching.
screen: `A TOWN, NOT THE CAPITAL.` → `A PRIEST AND FIVE SONS.` → `GO FIRST, AND BE THE KING'S FRIEND.`

segments.voice: He answers loudly, so the whole crowd hears: even if every nation in the king's realm obeys and abandons the ways of its ancestors, I and my sons and my brothers will walk in the covenant of our fathers. Then the story turns violent. Another Jew steps up to offer the sacrifice. Mattathias, burning with zeal, kills him at the altar, kills the king's officer too, and pulls the altar down. The book compares him to Phinehas, the zealous priest in Numbers. It's a hard scene, and some readers are uneasy with it; the book offers no apology. Then Mattathias calls through the town for anyone zealous for the law and faithful to the covenant to follow him, and he and his sons flee to the mountains, leaving everything. Some later Hanukkah retellings put an older cry in his mouth, the call Moses made at the golden calf. In the King James words: "Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me." In Hebrew, mi la-Adonai elai. Then a turn that's easy to miss. Some of the faithful hide in the wilderness, the enemy attacks them on the Sabbath, and they refuse even to block the caves. They die, the text says, with their families. When Mattathias hears, he and his friends decide: if anyone attacks us on the Sabbath, we will fight back, or we'll all be wiped out. Refusing the king also meant choosing to stay alive, so the covenant would still have people to keep it.
screen: `I AND MY SONS WILL WALK IN THE COVENANT.` · `THE ALTAR PULLED DOWN.` · then, large: `WHO IS ON THE LORD'S SIDE?` · `FIGHTING BACK ON THE SABBATH.`

segments.voice: Think of one small wrong you're being invited to join, a rumor at work, a joke at somebody's expense, a shortcut that cheats someone, and picture the moment the invitation comes, with everyone watching. Hear yourself say no, calmly, in one short sentence, until it feels like yours. If you pray, ask in words from your tradition for steadiness.
Mattathias. The priest of Modi'in who refused the king's sacrifice, called the faithful to follow, and began the revolt. Today's word.
Your line: who is for the lord. He said no aloud, with the whole town watching. Day eight hundred ninety-two.

howItsDone: At Hanukkah, Jews add the Al HaNissim passage to their prayers, which names Mattathias son of Yohanan, the Hasmonean high priest, and his sons.

original.note: Hebrew: whoever is for the Lord, to me. Moses's call in Exodus 32:26, which some later Hanukkah retellings give to Mattathias.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Maccabee revolt began with an army.
what it means: it began with a priest in a town outside the capital who said no out loud, then fled to the hills with his sons.
what a scholar hears: 1 Maccabees 2 compares him to Phinehas and gives his own call; the Hebrew cry mi la-Adonai elai comes from Exodus 32:26 and later retellings.

chat.says: Why did Mattathias and his followers decide to fight back even on the Sabbath?
options: After Sabbath-day attackers killed the faithful, they chose to fight so the covenant would survive.
They decided the Sabbath laws no longer counted at all once the king had banned them.
They wanted to show the king they cared more about winning battles than the Sabbath.
chat.meaning: 1 Maccabees 2: faithful people who wouldn't fight on the Sabbath were killed, so Mattathias decided to fight back, so the covenant would still have people.

notes: 1 Maccabees 2 paraphrased: Modin and the five sons (2:1–5); mourning (2:14); officers' offer (2:17–18); answer (2:19–22, paraphrased, not quoted); killing at the altar and comparison to Phinehas (2:23–26); the call to follow (2:27); the Sabbath massacre and decision to fight (2:29–41).

The carry 'who is for the lord' renders mi la-Hashem elai (Exodus 32:26), which Jewish retellings (e.g. some Hanukkah tellings and liturgical poems) attribute to Mattathias; 1 Maccabees 2:27 has a different wording. The script says 'Jewish retellings put an older cry in his mouth'; please confirm this is fair and cite a specific retelling if possible.
The original uses ה׳ for the divine name and the pronunciation 'Adonai' as read in Jewish practice; please confirm the Keeper's preference (some prefer 'Hashem' outside prayer).
The violence at the altar is stated plainly with 'some readers are uneasy with it'; Keeper please check tone.
